candidate_relations.reason: Normal fibrinogen, absent schistocytes, and isolated thrombocytopenia conflict with DIC as the platelet mechanism.
Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are presenting symptoms, not the thrombocytopenia diagnosis.
TTP is unsupported without schistocytes or a MAHA picture.
Sepsis/bacteremia is present but omits C. canimorsus and immune thrombocytopenia.
Bacteremia is a component missing organism and ITP.
Capnocytophaga canimorsus infection names the dog-bite pathogen but omits immune thrombocytopenia.
Daily wine and macrocytosis suggest alcoholic liver disease as comorbidity, not the acute ITP mechanism.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation remains incompatible with the coagulation/smear findings.
No murmur or vegetations are described; infective endocarditis is not established.
TTP remains an incompatible microangiopathic mechanism.

case_quality_flags: Dog-bite fusiform Gram-negative bacteremia with isolated thrombocytopenia, normal fibrinogen, and no schistocytes supports C. canimorsus-induced immune thrombocytopenia; no candidate includes both organism and ITP.
